title: Streaming + function-call cross-version compatibility pipeline with golden fingerprints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a robust cross-version regression pipeline that validates API compatibility for streaming responses, function/tool-call outputs, and structured JSON outputs. This ticket implements a deterministic 'golden fingerprint' approach plus tolerant matchers so CI can catch regressions without being brittle. Compatibility regressions have been the top source of downstream customer incidents; this pipeline aims to reduce false positives while surfacing developer-actionable failures (model-shim mismatches, tokenizer shifts, chunking differences).
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI job 'compatibility-regress' runs on every model rollout and returns pass/fail with detailed mismatch artifacts. 2) Golden fingerprint set (per API surface: streaming/text, stream+tool, structured JSON, embeddings) is stored and versioned in S3 with provenance metadata. 3) Matchers tolerate chunk boundary splits, whitespace/tokenization noise, and ordering invariants for function arguments. 4) Flaky-test detector highlights tests with >10% transient failure rate and automatically marks them flaky for manual review. 5) Runbooks and rebaseline checklist published in Confluence and linked from CI failure emails.
test_plan: Create a canonical corpus of 120 golden prompts across the following buckets: short-turn streaming, long generation streaming, tool function call with nested args, structured JSON with optional fields, and edge-case tokens (unicode, long tokens).

Implement fingerprinting: tokenized normalized hashes, JSON canonicalization + stable key ordering, and stream-chunk-aware cumulative fingerprints. Store artifacts under s3://redwood-ci/compatibility/goldens/runtime-2.4/.
Create tolerant matchers: exact-json, schema-validate, fuzzy-text (levenshtein threshold + token-union), and stream-chunk-merge algorithm to reassemble tool calls split across frames.
Build CI jobs: compatibility-regress (full), compatibility-canary (subset on push to model-versions), nightly-compat-smoke for quick regression detection.
Add instrumentation to capture token-level diffs, model version, tokenizer checksum, serving-kernel variant, and runtime config for every failed case.
Implement automated rebaseline proposal PR generator that submits candidate golden updates with diff summary and links to failing traces for reviewer approval.
Integrate flaky detection stats into Console to show per-test historical pass rates and link to recent CI builds for triage.
Add guardrails to fail CI only on high-confidence compatibility regressions (threshold configurable by label/team).
test_cases: TC-01: Streaming response where model emits function_call.name in mid-stream then later emits args across multiple chunks -> reconstructed and validated against golden.
TC-02: Function-call param ordering: same args in different order should match schema-valid fuzzy comparator.
TC-03: Structured JSON with optional null fields and additional vendor keys; comparator uses JSON Schema + allow-additional-keys flag for legacy clients.
TC-04: Long-stream token-splitting: expected token splitting behavior across buffers; tolerant matcher should rejoin sub-token fragments.
TC-05: Non-deterministic tokens: timestamps/UUIDs masked via redactors before fingerprinting.
TC-06: Backwards-compat check when model quantization changes kernel -> ensure no semantic change to function-call args or structured fields.
TC-07: Canary run on runtime-2.4 candidate model build to validate zero-downtime fallback and identical tool-call contract shapes.
TC-08: Flaky detection: introduce transient network delay to confirm flaky classification logic flags test if intermittent.
steps: 1. Finalize golden corpus and store source prompts in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/compatibility/tree/main/goldens/.
2. Implement fingerprint library in infra repo (Go) with stable tokenizer interface and JSON canonicalizer.
3. Add CI pipeline YAML and test runner harness that records artifacts to S3 and posts summary to Slack/Console.
4. Create automated PR bot to propose rebaselines with change rationale and diff artifacts.
5. Ship the first full run for runtime-2.4; triage failures and create follow-ups for true regressions vs matcher tuning.
6. Publish runbook and ownership matrix for on-call engineers and product reviewers.

risks: False positives due to tokenizer drift could erode trust in pipeline; mitigation: add tokenizer checksum and tighten matcher classification with human-in-loop rebaselines.
Storage costs for retaining full artifacts across model versions; mitigation: compress artifacts and keep 90-day hot window then archive.

Automated rebaseline PRs could accidentally approve behavioral regressions if reviewers become desensitized; mitigation: require at least one cross-team approver and link to customer-impact heuristics.
Long CI runtime for full corpus could slow development; mitigation: run small canary on push and full suite nightly with failure gating thresholds.
